acceptance.given: A capability performs database writes and its capability contract is authored or validated.

oracle.expected: The contract declares transaction and failure-handling behavior and identifies where the owning workflow records real backup/restore results.
forbidden: A database-write capability omits failure-handling behavior.
Static validation is presented as a restore drill.
oracle.observable: The capability contract contains explicit failure-handling behavior and an owning-workflow location for real backup/restore results.

acceptance.then: The contract’s failure-handling and real-result recording declarations are observable during static validation.
acceptance.when: Static validation inspects the database-write capability contract.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Evaluate a database-write capability contract with transaction or failure-handling behavior omitted; validation must fail.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Require database-write capability contracts to declare transaction/failure handling and where the owning workflow records real backup/restore results.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Reverting the standard removes this authoring requirement; no runtime state or schema is changed.

slice_hint.state_transition: The database-write capability contract gains explicit failure-handling and real backup/restore result-recording declarations.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Static contract validation observes the required failure-handling and result-recording declarations.

acceptance.given: A capability has no database-write or other database behavior.

oracle.expected: Scope validation imposes no database or backup-system prerequisite on the capability.
forbidden: A non-database capability is required to provide or depend on a database or backup system.
oracle.observable: The capability-aware scope check reports no database/backup prerequisite for the non-database capability.

acceptance.then: The scope check’s result imposes no database or backup-system requirement.
acceptance.when: The package validator evaluates the capability’s declared scope.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Evaluate a capability with no database behavior against a scope check that imposes a database or backup-system prerequisite; the check must fail.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Do not impose database or backup-system prerequisites on capabilities without database behavior.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Reverting the standard removes this scope rule; no runtime state or schema is changed.

slice_hint.state_transition: Scope evaluation of a capability without database behavior yields no database or backup prerequisite.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Scope validation observes that a non-database capability has no database or backup-system prerequisite.

acceptance.given: Submitted recovery evidence contains a fabricated “already verified” declaration instead of real restore-drill evidence.

oracle.expected: Validation rejects the declaration as insufficient recovery verification evidence.
forbidden: A fabricated “already verified” declaration is accepted as verification evidence.
Static validation is counted as a restore drill.
oracle.observable: The recovery-verification validator returns a failure identifying the fabricated declaration as invalid evidence.

acceptance.then: The validator rejects the fabricated declaration.
acceptance.when: The recovery-verification validator evaluates the submitted evidence.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Submit recovery evidence containing only a fabricated “already verified” declaration to the recovery-verification validator; validation must fail.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Reject fabricated “already verified” declarations as recovery evidence; static validation does not establish a restore drill.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Reverting the standard removes this evidence rule; no runtime state or schema is changed.

slice_hint.state_transition: Fabricated recovery-verification evidence is rejected rather than treated as a completed restore drill.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The recovery-verification check returns failure for the fabricated declaration.
